text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- The President of the Republic speaks the language of truth on the Cyprus issue. There has been no decision yet for the permanent deployment of planes in Paphos.
- Eighty-one percent of viewers were satisfied with Clerides's answers, according to a telephone poll by Logos TV.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Clerides hedges on Greek warplanes. "We have not taken a decision on whether the planes will stay here."
- The Grey Wolves group "is just a young people's club", says Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Charalambides rejects Woolworth takeover bid.
- Brokers are at odds with the finance minister over the prevailing negative mood on the Cyprus stock market.
- Lombard NatWest Cyprus profits doubled in 1996 to 3.28 million pounds from 1.64 million.
HARAVGHI
- Over-hyped news conference by Clerides turned into an academic debate.
- Snow falls to the lowlands.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Suitors for the presidential elections increase with the likelihood of party alliances in the first round.
- Sek trade union says unemployment reached 4.3 percent in January.
SIMERINI
- The United Nations prepare ideas to bridge key differences between the two sides.
- Proposal to ban overflights was a Turkish suggestion adopted by the U.S.
